brief: A cover to hide the cables behind my TV and keep them tidy.

requirements.evidence: 3 full bases in a row (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full) with full top covers and capped open side faces form an enclosed trunk; cable-coil prop staged on the deck shows cables routed along it
requirements.requirement: Cover to hide cables behind TV

requirements.evidence: 2x cable comb accessories, zip-tie anchor insert, 2x cable gland ports at the trunk ends keep the bundle ordered and give entries/exits

finish.summary: 3-cell enclosed cable trunk with top covers, end cable-gland entries, internal cable combs and zip anchor, staged with coiled cable.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Tidying those TV cables into a hidden cover — let me design a neat channel.
